domain: Constitutional Law / Political Sociology / International Relations
topic_summary: Analysis of the Hong Kong National Security Law as a contested kernel where Beijing's reading (sovereign security restoration) and civic/international reading (democratic enclosure mechanism) instantiate structurally different constraints from the same legal text. The NSL criminalizes secession, subversion, terrorism, and collusion with foreign forces, with mainland-style enforcement apparatus transplanted into Hong Kong's common law system.

key_entities: Central People's Government (CPG) — ultimate interpretive authority via NPCSC
Hong Kong SAR Government — local enforcement apparatus
Office for Safeguarding National Security (mainland agency in HK)
International observers (UN Human Rights Council, US/UK/EU)
One Country Two Systems framework (50-year autonomy promise, 1997-2047)
key_tensions: Sovereign security vs autonomy preservation (CPG vs 1C2S promise)
National security vs civil liberties (NSL enforcement vs common law tradition)
Mainland jurisdiction vs HK legal system (mainland judges in NSL cases vs local judiciary)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The Hong Kong National Security Law text itself — a codified legal instrument claiming to restore order and sovereignty while maintaining One Country Two Systems
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Dual structure: NPCSC holds final interpretive authority (mainland constitutional supremacy) while HK courts apply the law (common law tradition). Interpretive legitimacy contested between sovereignty claims and treaty/autonomy commitments.

readings.commitment: NSL as legitimate sovereign security instrument restoring constitutional order after 2019 unrest
readings.authority_grounding: Parliamentary sovereignty (NPCSC supremacy) + Westphalian territorial integrity
readings.expected_structural_delta: Protesters/activists enter victim set as security threats; CPG authority enters beneficiary set; extractiveness moderate (targets political opposition, not general population)

readings.commitment: NSL as mechanism for permanent closure of democratic space and criminalization of dissent
readings.authority_grounding: Human rights law + treaty obligation (Sino-British Joint Declaration) + autonomy promise
readings.expected_structural_delta: Civil society/press/opposition enter victim set; Beijing/HK establishment enter beneficiary set; extractiveness high (suppresses entire democratic infrastructure)

readings.commitment: NSL as vehicle for mainland legal system transplantation, eroding common law autonomy
readings.expected_structural_delta: HK judiciary/legal profession enter victim set; mainland security apparatus enters beneficiary set; extractiveness moderate-high (captures institutional independence)

axiom_contradictions.basis: Sovereignty_restoration axiom: state security threats are objectively identifiable and warrant coercive suppression. Democratic_enclosure axiom: political opposition is categorically distinct from security threats and warrants protection. No framework can hold both — accepting one requires rejecting the other's threat/dissent boundary.

Democratic_enclosure focuses on political rights suppression as primary harm. Jurisdictional_capture focuses on institutional autonomy erosion. These are NOT axiom-contradictory — a pluralist framework can hold both (rights depend on institutional independence). Coexist_with edge but no contradiction declaration.

omegas.description: Can any single legal framework simultaneously hold sovereignty_restoration's 'security threat identification' axiom and democratic_enclosure's 'dissent protection' axiom? The axiom contradiction indicates NO — but both readings persist as socially live positions. This is licensed plurality: the kernel sustains contradictory interpretations without resolution mechanism.

Will jurisdictional_capture_reading remain distinct from sovereignty_restoration_reading as mainland legal transplantation becomes normatively complete? If HK judiciary fully adopts mainland interpretation norms, the two readings may collapse into one.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (temporal stability of reading independence)

omegas.description: Democratic_enclosure_reading identifies 'civil society/press/opposition' as victim set. Does this include ordinary citizens engaging in private dissent, or only organized opposition? Boundary ambiguity affects extractiveness classification (high vs very high).

Is the 50-year autonomy promise (1997-2047) a Mountain (treaty obligation with international law status) or a Piton (revocable political commitment)? China's position: Sino-British Joint Declaration is 'historical document' with no ongoing force. UK/international position: binding treaty. Classification uncertainty affects whether 1C2S atrophy is constraint violation or constraint reclassification.

If Beijing withdrew NSL enforcement tomorrow, would civil society/press spontaneously reconstitute? Or has 4+ years of extraction created irreversible emigration/self-censorship? Reversibility determines whether this is Snare (trapping mechanism) or Tangled_Rope (coercive coordination with exit penalty).
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (beneficiary scan + mechanism reversibility)

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: one_country_two_systems_atrophy classified as piton but could be mountain (treaty obligation) depending on international law interpretation. Generated omega_1c2s_mountain_validity to bound this uncertainty. Also: kernel decomposition successful — three readings instantiate genuinely different victim/beneficiary structures from same legal text, meeting §1.3-K criteria.
